approach: int param copied to local, compared via local (many variants: temp var, u32, pointer indirection)
diff_signature: target 'adds r4,r0,#0; cmp r4,#4' vs MWCC 'adds r4,r0,#0; cmp r0,#4' at function entry
lesson: MWCC copy-propagates parameter copies back to r0 in comparisons; 'cmp r4' after a param copy only occurs for saved return values (after a bl). Pure C cannot produce this — use NONMATCHING inline asm.

lesson: -ipa file CSEs repeated static-data addresses across call sites regardless of linkage; making functions non-static does NOT disable IPA. Original source must have had a structure that prevented this — unknown.

approach: Faithful u8 buf[2] little-endian combine: buf[0]=unk04[i]; buf[1]=unk08[i]; return buf[0]|(buf[1]<<8)
diff_signature: MWCC -O4,p SCALARIZES the buffer (46B vs asm 54B): removes stack buf, hoists count-1 into callee-saved reg, adds u16 truncation mask. asm keeps a real stack buffer with a DEAD store of buf[1] (proves escape) and reloads a->unk0C every iteration (no hoist).
lesson: asm is the LESS-optimized form; need to DEFEAT MWCC scalarization+hoisting, not write cleaner C.

approach: Force buffer to memory via early 'u8 *q=buf;' before loop; also tried late q=buf and 'u16 ret' byte-pointer backing
diff_signature: early q=buf reproduces stack buffer+dead store (24 diffs, sizes match) but q lives in a callee-saved reg across loop => MWCC hoists count-1 into ANOTHER callee-saved reg + adds u16 mask. asm computes buf addr LATE in scratch (add r1,sp,#0 post-loop), no hoist, no mask. late q=buf re-scalarizes; u16 ret backing => 58B.
lesson: Could not reproduce asm's exact register allocation (late-scratch buf addr + no-hoist). Genuine regalloc match; left as asm.

diff_signature: vs old reverted C (p declared first): only diff was r2<->r3 swap (p in r2/i in r3 vs asm p in r3/i in r2). Swapping decl order so i is declared first flips allocation to i->r2, p->r3.
lesson: For two same-lifetime locals competing for r2/r3, MWCC assigns the FIRST-DECLARED to the lower register. Declaration order is a reg-alloc lever.

approach: Re-apply old save-chunk C but IPA-safe: split-header (new self-sufficient _internal.h for struct), frozen shared header + save_arrays.c untouched, local fwd decls for public fns
lesson: When the shared header is frozen struct-only (no global.h) it cannot be a .c main header (clang-format forces main header first, before global.h, so u8 is undefined). Use a differently-named self-sufficient _internal.h: clang-format then sorts global.h (P2) ahead of it. save_arrays.o stayed byte-identical => zero IPA cascade.
